channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: China: Credit demand and liquidity trends – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research anticipates China’s credit demand to stay weak in July, with new Yuan loans around RMB 10.8 billion and M2 growth at 8% year-on-year. Corporate and household medium- to long-term lending are likely to soften amid cautious borrowing and mortgage prepayments.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Range trade holds with bullish tone against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann see USD/CNH confined to a narrow intraday range, with flat momentum suggesting consolidation between 6.7450 and 6.7550.

item.title: Singapore: GDP revision and forecast upgrade – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research expects Singapore’s final 2Q26 GDP to be revised up to 5.9% year-on-year and 1.3% quarter-on-quarter seasonally adjusted, driven by stronger manufacturing and services.

item.title: Hormuz deal hopes rise as talks progress – Reuters
item.description: A US official said on Friday that there is progress in Oman-Iran talks and that a deal could be signed soon, according to Reuters. Once the deal is announced, this would restore commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, and the US would lift the blockade.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Rebound holds above 200-day SMA
item.description: The British Pound retreats against the Japanese Yen, down about 0.24%, as the Yen is poised to end the week on a higher note. However, GBP/JPY is poised to finish the week with minimal gains, trading at 212.64.

item.title: Philippines: BSP policy outlook shifts – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Jonathan Koh and Edward Lee now expect Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to keep its policy rate unchanged at the 27 August meeting, abandoning a previously projected hike.

item.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: US inflation takes center stage next week
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) fell below the 100.00 region after sinking through Friday's session. July Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) showed the US economy shedding 23K jobs against forecasts of an 80K gain, with June revised down to 20K, and Average Hourly Earnings slowing to 3.2% on the year.

item.title: US Treasury yields drop on soft NFP, Hormuz hopes ease Fed risks
item.description: US Treasury yields drop across the curve on Friday amid growing speculation that the Iran-Oman deal is about to be sealed, which has so far pushed energy prices lower, while investors also digest a weak Nonfarm Payrolls report in the US.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Supportive domestic backdrop, capped gains – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s FX analysts, including Charlie Lay and Moses Lim, note that USD/IDR slipped slightly but stayed below the key 18,000 level as softer global Oil prices and stronger Indonesia Q2 GDP supported the Rupiah.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD clears 50-day SMA, eyes $65
item.description: Silver price surges nearly 3% as it clears the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at $62.13, and reclaims the $63.00 figure as it struggles to surpass key resistance seen at $63.28, the July 6 high.

item.title: EUR/JPY recovers from session low but remains down on Friday
item.description: EUR/JPY trades on the back foot on Friday, easing away even as the Euro (EUR) posts solid gains against the US Dollar (USD). The Japanese currency surged suddenly near the start of the American session after a surprisingly weak United States (US) employment report.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Bulls need 1.3560 to unlock 1.3600
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) edges higher by some 0.29% against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, yet it remains trading sideways, unable to decisively crack 1.3500 after reaching a three-week peak of 1.3509, and has retreated to the 1.3490 area.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Upside risk capped by 1.2790 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/SGD has firmed modestly, with the pair closing at 1.2835 after testing both 1.2800 and 1.2840. Short-term momentum now favors a mild upside, though strong resistance at 1.2850 is expected to cap gains.

item.title: Mexican Peso hits five-month high on weak US jobs data
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) capitalizes on a weaker US jobs report and soars versus the US Dollar (USD) on Friday as risk appetite improves and the Greenback gets battered on speculation that the Federal Reserve (Fed) might not raise rates in 2026.

item.title: South Korean Won: Intervention risks support KRW against US Dollar – DBS
item.description: Chang Wei Liang at DBS Group Research notes that KRW is currently the best performing Asian currency, supported by strong semiconductor demand and reported FX intervention coordination between Korea, the US and Japan.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Buyers eye a break above the 100-day SMA
item.description: EUR/USD edges higher on Friday, supported by a softer US Dollar (USD) as traders scale back Federal Reserve (Fed) rate-hike bets following a disappointing US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1562, hovering near a seven-week high.

item.title: Gold rallies as mediocre US NFP crushes Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) skyrockets on Friday, gaining over 2.30% in the day and more than 7% in the week after US jobs data was mixed, with a softer Nonfarm Payrolls print while the Unemployment Rate remained steady.

item.title: Indonesia: Modest growth outlook – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Aldian Taloputra notes Indonesia’s Q2 GDP grew 5.3% year-on-year, slowing from 5.6% but beating consensus. Stronger-than-expected H1 data leads the bank to raise its 2026 GDP forecast to 5.3%.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average dodges a hike December still prices
item.description: The American labour market contracted in July and the Dow Jones Industrial Average answered with a gain of roughly 65 points, a tenth of a percent, trading near 54,000 into the afternoon.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar advances as US labor market weakness pressures USD
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5890 on Friday at the time of writing, up 0.36% on the day.

item.title: Canada: Gradual improvement with tariff risks – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada’s (RBC) Nathan Janzen reports that Canada’s labour market strengthened in July, with a 75k employment gain following robust increases in May and June and a decline in the unemployment rate to 6.4%.

item.title: Australian Dollar climbs near two-month highs as NFP turns negative
item.description: The AUD/USD pair surged to its highest in nearly two months past 0.7070 earlier on Friday, following the release of the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report. The move owes nothing to Australia.

item.title: NY Fed inflation expectations ease modestly in the short term
item.description: The New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations shows that households’ inflation expectations decreased slightly over the short-term horizon and remained unchanged at the medium and longer-term horizons. One-year inflation expectations eased from 3.7% in June to 3.6% in July

item.title: Natural Gas: Higher price forecasts on LNG squeeze – Commerzbank
item.description: Norman Liebke at Commerzbank has revised Gas and German power price forecasts higher, citing tighter European storage, increased reliance on LNG and structural constraints on Qatari exports. The phase-out of Russian Gas from 2027 adds upside risk.

item.title: US Dollar: Payrolls-driven consolidation as CPI looms – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that the US Dollar (USD) weakened after the disappointing July Payrolls report, but see limited downside against G10 currencies unless softer US inflation further reduces Fed hike expectations.

item.title: Gold heads for best week since January after disappointing NFP
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its recovery on Friday as weaker-than-expected US payroll growth weighs on the US Dollar (USD) and US Treasury yields. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,356 after hitting $4,371, its highest level since June 17.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Fed focus shifts to jobs – ABN AMRO
item.description: ABN AMRO’s Chief Economist Nick Kounis highlights renewed US labour market weakness, with Nonfarm Payrolls falling and household employment data softening. He notes the unemployment rate declined as labour force participation dropped to multi-decade lows, signalling cyclical weakness.

item.title: Swiss Franc gains against US Dollar after surprise decline in US payrolls
item.description: USD/CHF edges lower on Friday, erasing most of the previous day’s gains as the US Dollar (USD) weakens following a downside surprise in the US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.8080, down 0.53% on the day.

item.title: Canada: Labour market resilience supports cautious Bank of Canada – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada (NBC) economists Matthieu Arseneau and Alexandra Ducharme highlight robust Canadian labour data for July, with 75.1K jobs added, a lower unemployment rate and stronger private-sector hiring.

item.title: Gold: Discretionary demand keeps bulls in control - TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists Ryan McKay and Bart Melek highlight that strong discretionary and Asian buying is supporting Gold, even as CTA (Commodity Trading Advisors) positioning has plateaued.
